title: Nutrition Department Terms on Ration Changes, Farm Visits and Analyses
content:
A ration is changed on the nutritionist's written instruction and not on a telephone call from the yard, because the formula on file is what the mill is obliged to run. Within the Feed and Animal Nutrition Programmes a change needs the programme's notice in calendar days before the new formula is run, and the mill finishes any load already batched on the old formula.

## What the programme carries and what it charges

The programme carries a number of changes a year at no charge, counted over the calendar year, and a change beyond that count carries the programme's change charge. The count the desk works from is the number of ration changes recorded on that programme within the current calendar year.

Nutritionist visits and laboratory analyses beyond the counts the programme includes are charged at the programme's rates.

## Moves that are not ordinary ration changes

Moving between an unmedicated and a medicated formula is not an ordinary ration change at all and needs a current directive of its own.

Where a change moves between incompatible additives the bin is cleaned out first at the programme's cleanout charge, and that charge is raised whether or not the member asked for the cleanout, because the mill will not run the new formula into a contaminated bin.

## Points of judgement

| The change asked for | How it is treated |
| --- | --- |
| A change within the number the programme carries in the calendar year | Made at no charge |
| A change beyond that number in the same calendar year | The programme's change charge is raised |
| A change from one unmedicated formula to another with incompatible additives | The bin is cleaned out first, at the programme's cleanout charge, asked for or not |
| A change from an unmedicated formula to a medicated one | Not an ordinary ration change; a current directive of its own is called for |

*Hypothetical.* A programme carrying two changes in the year has had two recorded since the first of January. A third asked for in December of the same year is beyond the count and carries the programme's change charge; the count starts again with the new calendar year.

*Hypothetical.* A written instruction reaches the mill on the tenth of a month on a programme taking three calendar days of notice. The new formula is run from the thirteenth, and a load already batched on the old formula on the eleventh is finished as batched.
